parsed.headline: Advance voting for Toronto's 2026 municipal election ends Sunday

pages.text: Advance voting for the 2026 municipal election in Toronto, Canada, is scheduled to conclude this Sunday at 7 p.m. According to the city, the advance voting period began on October 6, 2026, with polls opening at 10 a.m. The voting process is available at 50 locations in total, representing two locations in each ward. Residents who requested to vote by mail must return their completed voting packages to Toronto Elections by October 14 at noon. Following the conclusion of advance voting, the next opportunity to vote will be on election day, October 26, from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m.

Voters using the municipal ballot will select candidates for mayor, councillor, and school board trustee by filling in an oval. The city stated in an October 5 news release that a voter may only vote once, regardless of how many properties they own or rent in Toronto, and must vote in the ward where they live. To be eligible, a person must be a Canadian citizen, at least 18 years old, a resident of Toronto, and not prohibited from voting under any law. Non-residents may vote if they or their spouse own or rent property in the city. The city has indicated that information regarding turnout for the advance voting period will be released on October 6, 2026.

parsed.headline: President Mahama projects Bechem, Ghana, will become the country's chicken capital

pages.text: President John Dramani Mahama projected that the town of Bechem in the Ahafo Region will become the chicken capital of Ghana once the Poultry, Meat and Feed Processing Plant becomes operational. During an inspection of the project, which is reported to be 50 per cent complete, the President noted that the facility is expected to be ready for commissioning by the end of the first quarter of 2027. The inspection was part of the first day of the President's two-day Resetting Ghana Tour of the Ahafo Region. The President, who officially cut the sod for the modern poultry, meat, and feed processing plant on November 27, 2025, commended the project consultants, Architecture and Engineering Services Limited (AESL), for the progress made. He stated that the factory would create jobs and advised local youth to enter poultry farming to utilize the ready market. Mahama noted that the Nkoko Nketenkete initiative was started prior to the factory construction to ensure a sufficient poultry supply for processing. Following the launch of the Nkoko Nketenkete initiative under the Feed Ghana Programme, Minister of Food and Agriculture Eric Opoku stated that Ghana’s domestic poultry production increased from 4.6 per cent to 22 per cent as of May 2026.

parsed.headline: Trump calls for Ukraine to elect a new president to end war with Russia

pages.text: U.S. President Donald Trump called on Saturday for Ukraine to elect a new president, stating that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has failed to reach an agreement to end the war with Russia. Speaking at the White House, Trump suggested that Ukraine needs a leader capable of making a peace deal, alleging that Zelenskyy has missed many opportunities to settle the conflict. According to reports from The Associated Press and Anadolu Agency, Trump claimed Zelenskyy could have settled the war many times but has chosen not to. Trump also stated that Zelenskyy has lost 30% of the country and that over 2 million people have been killed in the war, which he characterized as a conflict that should never have started. Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Trump’s remarks followed his criticism of Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure, specifically oil refineries. He argued that such attacks could worsen diesel fuel shortages and negatively impact American farmers and ranchers. Trump claimed he told Ukraine to do what they want but instructed them not to hit diesel fuel due to a significant shortage. On October 9, 2026, Trump announced an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin for Russia to supply diesel to U.S. and global markets to lower fuel prices, an action accompanied by his administration's temporary easing of sanctions on Russian fuel exports. Kyiv has criticized this agreement, warning that allowing Russian diesel exports could provide Moscow with additional revenue while the war continues.

parsed.headline: Ghanaian Minority caucus demands audit of GH¢49.72 million South Africa evacuation spending

pages.text: The Minority caucus in Ghana has called for an independent audit of a GH¢49.72 million evacuation exercise, alleging that records provided by the Foreign Affairs Ministry leave more than GH¢16.4 million requiring further explanation. Nana Asafo-Adjei Ayeh, the Deputy Ranking Member of Parliament of the Foreign Affairs Committee and MP for Bosome-Freho, presented these allegations following a review of documents provided by Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa in response to a Right to Information request. The Minority argues that the records do not fully reconcile with the government’s reported expenditure and a total of 1,964 evacuees. The allegations include discrepancies involving reintegration grants, transport allowances, commercial flight records, duplicate entries, and payments involving minors, though the claims do not establish that funds were stolen or that beneficiary numbers were deliberately inflated. The issues raised require verification of the underlying records and a response from the Ministry.

The evacuation exercise followed xenophobic violence and intimidation against foreign nationals in South Africa. According to the Ministry, the operation began on May 27 and concluded on September 4, 2026, when the final group of 41 returnees arrived in Ghana. On September 7, Minister Ablakwa announced a total expenditure of GH¢49,721,786, which consisted of GH¢33,721,786 in direct government funding and GH¢16 million in support attributed to Engineers & Planners, a company owned by businessman Ibrahim Mahama. The reported costs covered chartered flights, commercial airline tickets, ground transportation, feeding, accommodation, medical care, reintegration support, and other logistical expenses. The government stated that each evacuee received a GH¢5,000 reintegration grant and a GH¢500 transport allowance. While acknowledging the humanitarian importance of the operation, the Minority stated that its emergency nature did not relieve the government of the obligation to account for the funds spent.

parsed.headline: Bangladesh Home Minister to skip BIMSTEC ministerial meeting in Delhi

pages.text: Bangladesh Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed will not attend the first-ever meeting of home ministers from the seven-nation Bay of Bengal regional bloc, BIMSTEC, scheduled for October 6, 2026, in New Delhi, India. BIMSTEC Secretary General Indra Mani Pandey confirmed to Prothom Alo that while home ministers and state ministers from the other six member countries will participate, Bangladesh will be represented by a four-member delegation led by Home Ministry Senior Secretary Monzur Morshed Chowdhury. The decision was reflected in a diplomatic letter from the Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs sent to the BIMSTEC Secretariat on October 4, which listed the delegation for meetings on October 12 and 13 but excluded the home minister's name. Senior government officials, speaking anonymously, told Prothom Alo the decision was made in the context of ongoing strain in bilateral relations with India. This follows a September incident where Prime Minister Tarique Rahman did not attend a BRICS summit outreach session in Delhi; the Bangladesh government clarified that the invitation had been extended to him as the BIMSTEC chair rather than as Prime Minister.

The upcoming ministerial meeting in Delhi is expected to be chaired by Indian Home Minister Amit Shah, with a preceding meeting of senior home ministry officials on October 12 to be conducted by India's Home Secretary, Govind Mohan. Scheduled participants from other member states include Bhutan's Home Minister Lungten Dorji, Myanmar's Home Minister General Ko Ko Oo, Nepal's Home Minister Sudan Gurung, Sri Lanka's Home Minister Chandana Aberathne, and Thailand's Deputy Minister of Interior Songsak Thongsri. According to relevant sources, the meeting will focus on strengthening regional cooperation to combat terrorism and cross-border crime. Bangladesh assumed the chairmanship of BIMSTEC in April 2025. The seven-member bloc, which aims to bridge cooperation between South and South-East Asia, includes Bangladesh, India, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Nepal, and Bhutan.

parsed.headline: Albertans express varying views ahead of upcoming referendum

pages.text: Patrons at the Seton library branch of the Calgary Public Library in Alberta, Canada, shared diverse reactions to an upcoming referendum during a CBC News pop-up event. According to CBC News reporting, individuals expressed feelings ranging from excitement to frustration regarding the vote. Some participants expressed frustration at the existence of the vote, while others were still learning about the process and had not yet decided how to cast their ballots. One voter, Jim Fedor, stated he booked October 19 off work to participate in the referendum. Fedor told CBC News he intends to vote for Option 1 on the separation question to keep Alberta in Canada, and plans to vote no on the nine other questions.

parsed.headline: Nuclear war and malicious AI use pose extinction risks by 2100, Lancet assessment finds

pages.text: A new global risk assessment by The Lancet Commission on 21st Century Global Threats to Health identifies nuclear conflict and the malicious use of artificial intelligence as threats that could lead to human extinction within the next 75 years. The report states that nuclear conflict could potentially end humanity by injecting particles into the upper atmosphere to block sunlight and cause famine, while AI could be used to create biological weapons. Although the commission noted the likelihood of these specific events remains low, an accompanying editorial warned that their realization would inflict an apocalypse on humanity. 17 catastrophic threats to human health were identified by the commission, all of which were noted to have a “realistic route to act” upon. The commission modeled these threats based on disability-adjusted life years (Dalys), measuring potential years of healthy life lost due to sickness, disability, or early death. Other major catastrophic threats identified as potentially causing more than 1bn cumulative Dalys include climate breakdown, air pollution, antimicrobial resistance, childhood malnutrition, conventional conflict, declining overseas aid, high alcohol use, high blood pressure, income inequality, low educational attainment, naturally occurring pandemics, obesity, poor mental health, smoking, and unhealthy ageing.
